Indexing its result with [0]['id'] then raises before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Read the optional result safely and also handle a missing uncategorized_category_id setting."

      "body": "The old host-matching logic supported entries containing schemes and paths, such as https://example.com/1234. This INSERT copies those entries verbatim and bypasses EmbeddableHost's normalization callback. The new lookup compares the stored value with URI.host, so these migrated entries never match example.com. Existing embedded comments consequently return access errors and topic retrieval stops after upgrading. Normalize each legacy entry before inserting it."
    },

      "body": "Each legacy host value is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL literal. A URL containing an apostrophe in its path, such as https://example.com/it's, breaks the INSERT and aborts the upgrade; crafted values can also alter the SQL statement. Use bound values or connection.quote rather than treating persisted setting text as SQL."
    },

Legacy entries inserted by the migration bypass validation, but subsequently changing their category also fails validation. Hostname validation should not impose this obsolete TLD-length restriction."
    },

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Make port-qualified host storage and lookup consistent",
      "body": "Validation accepts example.com:8080, and normalization retains the port, including when an administrator enters https://example.com:8080. However, URI.host returns only example.com, which can never match the stored example.com:8080 value. A successfully saved port-qualified host therefore cannot embed comments or retrieve topics. Normalize storage and lookup consistently, or reject port-qualified entries explicitly."
    },

      "title": "Enforce one category mapping per normalized hostname",
      "body": "Neither the model nor the table prevents duplicate hostnames, including case variants. Administrators can save example.com twice with different categories, but record_for_host always selects the first matching row. Editing the other row succeeds without changing the category used for imports, leaving a configuration that the application silently ignores. Enforce case-insensitive hostname uniqueness in validation and the database."
    },

      "file": "app/models/embeddable_host.rb",

      "body": "The before_validation callback calls sub! on host without checking for nil. Creating or updating through the new endpoint with an omitted or null host therefore raises NoMethodError instead of returning the validation errors handled by save_host. The same exception occurs when validating EmbeddableHost.new. Guard normalization and validate the required host so malformed input produces a controlled error response."

findings.title: Handle an unset embed category before indexing the query result
findings.body: The category query returns no rows when embed_category was never configured or names a deleted or renamed category. Indexing its result with [0]['id'] then raises before reaching the uncategorized fallback. This prevents db:migrate from completing on installations that do not use embedding, including clean databases. Read the optional result safely and also handle a missing uncategorized_category_id setting.

findings.title: Normalize legacy hosts during migration
findings.body: The old host-matching logic supported entries containing schemes and paths, such as https://example.com/1234. This INSERT copies those entries verbatim and bypasses EmbeddableHost's normalization callback. The new lookup compares the stored value with URI.host, so these migrated entries never match example.com. Existing embedded comments consequently return access errors and topic retrieval stops after upgrading. Normalize each legacy entry before inserting it.

findings.title: Quote host values instead of interpolating them into SQL

A URL containing an apostrophe in its path, such as https://example.com/it's, breaks the INSERT and aborts the upgrade; crafted values can also alter the SQL statement. Use bound values or connection.quote rather than treating persisted setting text as SQL.

findings.title: Allow valid hostnames with longer top-level domains
findings.body: The hostname regex limits the final suffix to two through five letters, rejecting valid domains such as example.museum and example.technology. Administrators cannot add these hosts. Legacy entries inserted by the migration bypass validation, but subsequently changing their category also fails validation. Hostname validation should not impose this obsolete TLD-length restriction.

findings.title: Make port-qualified host storage and lookup consistent

However, URI.host returns only example.com, which can never match the stored example.com:8080 value. A successfully saved port-qualified host therefore cannot embed comments or retrieve topics. Normalize storage and lookup consistently, or reject port-qualified entries explicitly.

findings.title: Enforce one category mapping per normalized hostname
findings.body: Neither the model nor the table prevents duplicate hostnames, including case variants. Administrators can save example.com twice with different categories, but record_for_host always selects the first matching row. Editing the other row succeeds without changing the category used for imports, leaving a configuration that the application silently ignores. Enforce case-insensitive hostname uniqueness in validation and the database.

findings.title: Guard missing hosts before string normalization
findings.body: The before_validation callback calls sub! on host without checking for nil. Creating or updating through the new endpoint with an omitted or null host therefore raises NoMethodError instead of returning the validation errors handled by save_host.
